- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 2–5% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≤0.33), model often underestimates downside; add 3–8% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from 1.00 to -1.00), model fails to adjust quickly; apply 1–3 day lag correction to avoid overreacting to sentiment shifts.  
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d), model tends to overestimate volatility; cap forecast range within ±3% of 14-day moving average to avoid overfitting.  
- If true outcome deviates >10% from 14-day MA, re-weight sentiment influence: reduce bullish weight by 20% if sentiment is high, increase bearish weight by 20% if sentiment is low.
